questions.title: How steroid hormones signal
questions.question: Which of the following intracellular components is primarily involved in the signaling mechanism of steroid hormones?

options.A: The specialized surface membrane coupled G proteins
options.C: The completely external cell surface membrane receptors
options.D: The highly specific specialized tyrosine kinase enzymes

explanations.A: Incorrect. G protein-coupled receptors sit on the cell SURFACE and are used by water-soluble hormones, not lipid-soluble steroid hormones.
explanations.B: Correct. Because steroid hormones are lipid-soluble, they cross the plasma membrane freely rather than needing a surface receptor. They bind instead to intracellular receptors in the cytoplasm or nucleus. The hormone-receptor complex then acts directly on gene expression, which is why steroid effects are slower in onset but longer-lasting than peptide-hormone effects.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Surface membrane receptors are the mechanism for water-soluble peptide hormones, which cannot cross the membrane on their own — the opposite mechanism from a lipid-soluble steroid hormone.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Tyrosine kinase receptors are another surface-membrane mechanism, used by hormones such as insulin, not by lipid-soluble steroid hormones.

questions.learning_objective: State that steroid hormones signal through intracellular receptors because they are lipid-soluble.
